page.title: Best Ultrasonic Cutter for Resin Prints (2026): Sonic Saber vs NeoBlade vs WonderCutter
page.h1: Best ultrasonic cutter for resin prints
page.desc: Phrozen's $100 corded Sonic Saber is the best value for cutting resin supports. HOZO's $149 NeoBlade is better if you need cordless use or cut PLA. Prices checked 2026-11-11.
page.intro:
Short answer. The best ultrasonic cutter for resin prints is the Phrozen Sonic Saber ({buy:phrozen-sonic-saber-ultrasonic-cutter}): a corded pen cutter running at over 35,000 vibrations per second. Spare blades cost $10 for 20, about 50¢ each (Phrozen, 2026-11-11). Buyers' top worry is melting, but cured resin doesn't melt the way PLA does. Hackster's reviewer and owners report clean cuts on resin supports with a light touch, while one owner found PLA "almost impossible" to cut.

If you also trim PLA, foam or styrene, or want no cord, buy the HOZO NeoBlade instead. It costs $149 at HOZO (2026-11-11), adjusts its power from 9 to 40 W, and has a swappable battery that lasts about 30 minutes. In reviewers' tests it also melted PLA, so neither tool is a clean PLA cutter.

An ultrasonic cutter isn't essential for resin printing. It pays off if you print miniatures, busts or thin parts that snap when you use flush cutters.

page.after:
What owners complain about

  • Melting on FDM plastics (6 reports). Two Sonic Saber owners, two NeoBlade reviewers (CGMagazine, The Gadgeteer), a Proxxon owner and coverage of a newer cutter all describe heat smearing PLA or fusing cut pieces back together. Resin cuts cleanly. If PLA is your main job, a hot knife or flush cutters may serve you better.
  • A unit that died early (5). This came up for the Sonic Saber (2), NeoBlade (2) and an older WonderCutter that stopped cutting after a year. Phrozen and HOZO each replaced a unit under warranty. Test your cutter in the first week.
  • Slow or needs pressure (3). One Sonic Saber owner had to push hard on thin supports, a forum user found a NeoBlade "quite slow," and a WonderCutter struggled with a zip tie. Hackster found the opposite on thick resin supports. Fresh blades matter.
  • Cord vs battery (3). One owner switched to the NeoBlade because of a corded cutter's cord. CGMagazine's biggest NeoBlade complaint was its 30-minute battery, and The Gadgeteer's NeoBlade shut itself off after a few minutes of continuous use.
  • Bulk and noise (5). Three sources call cordless bodies thicker than a hobby knife. The NeoBlade's fan whine bothered one reviewer's spouse, and the Sonic Saber's vibration upset one reviewer's dog.

Which one by need

  • Resin miniatures and busts, working at a desk: Phrozen Sonic Saber. It costs the least, needs no charging, and its blades cost about 50¢ each.
  • Cordless, or you cut PLA, foam, styrene and leather too: HOZO NeoBlade. Its automatic 9–40 W power and six blade shapes cover more materials. Get the Creator Combo if you want a second battery.
  • Shop use on tough materials like carbon fiber: WonderCutter X, at 48 W and three power levels. At $799.95 it is overkill for resin supports.

Not recommended

  • Any ultrasonic cutter as your main PLA tool. Every one we read about melts PLA to some degree.
  • Crowdfunded cutters with no retail record, such as the SonicMax Slice 10 on Kickstarter. Its runtime and cooling claims haven't been tested independently yet.
  • Unbranded 40 kHz cutters. We couldn't confirm their specs, blade supply or warranty support, so we left them out.
